title: Catherine de' Medici to Paul de Foix, 15 Jan 1563, BL Add MS 4136 ff. 148v-149 (DECODE R9241)

documents.route: Catherine de' Medici to Paul de Foix, French ambassador in London (intercepted)

plaintext.source: not in Forbes ii, CSP Foreign vi, or La Ferrière, Lettres de Catherine de Médicis i-ii

transcription.notes: First pass, passages (1)-(4); some glyph classes (z/r, b variants) may be merged. f.148 top (passages 15-24) is the end of a Coligny letter and was not transcribed.

system.summary: Paul de Foix's own cipher (Tomokiyo's reconstruction from de Foix's 1565 letters): Latin letters, digits, ligatures and two-digit word signs, homophonic, with clear null words (pour, car); several signs two-valued.
system.notes: Clear French null words as in Throckmorton's third cipher, but the sign values do not match it. Coligny's graphic-sign cipher (R9238), once in this entry, is a different key (coligny1563).

prior_solution.where: No decipherment or clear copy of R9241 known (Forbes ii, CSP Foreign vi, La Ferrière i-ii searched); the key is Tomokiyo's reconstruction from other de Foix letters.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched R9238 and R9241 (2 images each) with the shared DECODE cookie.

Read the margins: f.142 'L'Amiral de France à la Reine d'Angleterre [1]2 Jan 1562/3'; f.148v 'La Reine-mère de France à Mr de Foix Ambass. en Angleterre 15 Jan 1563'. The two records are different letters.
Grepped Forbes ii OCR and CSP Foreign vi pp. 1-123: Coligny's letters to the Queen are 'almost entirely in cipher, deciphered' (nos. 7, 76) and printed by Forbes.

Margin glosses 'sins', 'desracine' at f.142 passage (9) match 'il rallie les siens ... desraciner du tout l'evangile' in the Villefranche letter of 12 Jan (Forbes ii 272-274), not the 2 Jan Meur letter: R9238 = CSP vi no. 76, read at the time.
Queen Mother to de Foix 15 Jan 1563 searched in Forbes ii, CSP Foreign vi and La Ferrière, Lettres de Catherine de Médicis i-ii: not found.
Compared R9241 with the Forbes key records: Throckmorton's first (R9260 p.2), second (R9260 p.3), third (R9262 p.1) and Croft's (R9261 p.2) ciphers.
Transcribed R9241 passages (1)-(4) into qm_tokens.txt: 952 tokens, 71 types, IoC 0.035.
Homophonic annealing with the shared lang dense 5-gram models (French, English): collapsed to runs of e/s; the model over-scores unseen repeats ('eeee' -0.26/char).
Joint-quadgram annealer (anneal3.py) on a 940-token synthetic homophonic control with 64 types: plaintext almost fully recovered.
anneal3.py on R9241 in French and English, with and without nulls: no language (about -9.8/char).
anneal3.py with Italian (Renaissance), Spanish (Quijote) and Latin corpora: no language.
Two tokens per letter: token parity within each passage is flat, so the hypothesis is not supported.
anneal3.py SYL=1: tokens map to a letter or one of 30 French bigrams; no language.
Second pass, sign by sign from full-resolution crops (two agents, one per page): qm2_tokens.txt, 1007 tokens, 92 types; splits of #/4t/H, 3/Z3, qs/qf, Lc/Yb, b/bB, D/Da and others.
anneal3.py on qm2_tokens.txt (French, English, French with nulls): no language.

Swept DECODE key records 1550-1580 with French plaintext (R335, R355, R331, R3818, R3820). R335 (Condé's cipher, 2 Dec 1562) matches R9238's signs: & and 14 nulls, ω = la Royne d'Angleterre in the heading line. None fits R9241.

Outside contribution, Lawrence Beck with ChatGPT (PR #18, folder beck-preliminary/): a 78-entry proposed key on a new 1,038-token transcription of R9241 (96 types; 1,013 tokens keyed). Decrypt is continuous period French in long stretches (la reconciliation necessaire entre ces deux royaumes; quelque deboursement de deniers dont nous n'avons nulle intention).

beck_control.py with lang fr-1600-letters (no spaces). Beck key -2.02/char vs 500 value-shuffled keys -4.28 +/- 0.39 (z 5.8). Overfitting control: swap-annealing a permutation of Beck's own 78 values on token-shuffled ciphertext reaches -1.93 to -2.00/char (per-char score is gameable by word-valued signs), but only 26-34% of letters in corpus words of 5+ letters against 50.6% for Beck's key on the real order (Beck's key on shuffled order: 4-7%). Independent check: 19 of 25 sign names shared with Feyseel's frozen key from de Foix's 1565 cipher (PR #21, Tomokiyo chart) give the same value, a 20th (6 = ie/je) agrees in effect. Real partial break, not at the read bar; 14 key entries rest on one occurrence each.

One-key split (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): catalogue 92's two records are in different ciphers. R9238 (Coligny to Elizabeth, 12 Jan 1563) is in the graphic-sign cipher of the Condé key R335, the same key as Coligny's other three letters of January 1563 in coligny1563 (R9237, R9239, R9240), so it moved there; foix1563 keeps R9241 (Catherine de' Medici to Paul de Foix), in de Foix's own cipher.

Catalogue audit: fraction_read had been set to 0.976, the share of tokens carrying a key value, which NOTES says is not a reading; set to the measured sense proxy (0.506, letters in 5+-letter corpus words) to match NOTES ('not at the read bar').

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): both proposed readings: Beck's (FRENCH_AND_ENGLISH.txt, literal.txt; his transcription restored from data/source.seed.xz to texts/beck_transcription.txt) and Nur's graded reading with the 1565 de Foix key, beside the project's qm/qm2 transcriptions (the exact token file Nur decoded is not in the folder)

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). Both proposed decodes read: Beck's French layer (FRENCH_AND_ENGLISH.txt) builds clauses in passages B and D ('son but seroit de nous faire entrer en quelque debourssement de deniers') but has gaps or unresolved letter strings in most sentences of A and C; his literal layer is unspaced letters with sporadic words; Nur's v5 rendering is fragments between ellipses (docs/_check_reading.py: 0-57% of sentences clean). Both entries relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read, method read after matching with key from external sources -> not solved (the key match kept as a part); fraction_read 0.506 -> 0.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b19): DECODE R9241 re-fetched: two images, no attachment, transcription or comment; both opened, no decipherment (Forbes copied only the cipher passages); neighbouring copies on ff. 148-149 are other letters (Coligny, Throckmorton). Print searched before (Forbes, CSP Foreign vi, La Ferriere).

Beck's key v13 combined with the 1565 cipher's word signs for the numbers he left open (10 dict, 26 bien, 34 tant, 40 faict, 70 toute, 82 ceulx, 37 me/car; each fits every occurrence) and the 1565 polyvalence f = u at two places (aussi, roiaulmes); b19_foix_decode.py, texts/R9241_decode.txt.

Every trouble spot checked on the DECODE photographs with Beck's line coordinates (A2, A4, A8, A12, A14-A16, B1, B3, C1-C2, D0, D6-D8): the signs are as Beck transcribed (his 20 in A8 is written 'zo'); no label changed. New: 'et ioue durant noz trouble le personnaige que vous scauez assez', 'aiant faict les [beaulx] [auancemens] de la [guere]', 'langaige accompaignee'. A2, A14-A16, B3, D7 and the closing name build no words under Beck's, the 1565 or Nur's fitted values.

Reading texts/R9241_reading.md with English (every unbracketed word carried, b19_wordcheck.py). Clean-sentence share: _check_reading.py 0.361; explicit holes only 0.609. Below the bar (French documents at 0.47-0.56 kept unread): R9241 stays decoded, not read, with this partial reading.

Method restored: key obtained by matching Paul de Foix's 1565 cipher (Tomokiyo; Beck's independent key agrees) (read after matching with key from external sources); text not read, class stays not read. The 22-24 Oct reading audit had set the method to not solved because the class was not read; George Lasry (24 Oct 2026) separates the two.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: R9241's signs match Paul de Foix's 1565 cipher (Tomokiyo's reconstruction; Feyseel Nur, PR #21), and Lawrence Beck's independent key (PR #18) agrees on 19 of 25 shared signs, but neither decode builds the letter into sentences: the key match is recorded in parts, the text is not read. Method restored 24 Oct 2026 (George Lasry: a key can be mostly recovered while the text is not read): the key was obtained by matching Paul de Foix's 1565 cipher (Tomokiyo; Beck's independent key agrees); class stays not read, as the text does not read.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: the one document does not build sentences in either proposed decode, so nothing counts as read (0). Withdrawn as a reading figure: 0.506, the share of letters of Beck's literal layer (beck-preliminary/results/literal.txt) falling in corpus words of 5+ letters (shuffled-key ceiling 34.2%), which measures word fragments, not sentences. 23 Oct 2026 (b19): the combined re-reading (Beck's key with the 1565 word signs, texts/R9241_reading.md) scores 0.361 on _check_reading.py (0.609 counting explicit holes only) and stays decoded, not read; fraction 0.

gaps.item: R9241 passages (1)-(4): the combined re-reading builds sentences in (2)-(4) but breaks twice in (1) (A2 "prolizgnaulx", A14-A16) and leaves B3, D7 and the closing name unread; clean-sentence share 0.361 (explicit holes 0.609)
gaps.detail: the open signs have no value in the 1565 chart (Tomokiyo, BnF fr. 15971) and no decipherment of a de Foix letter of 1563 is known; de Foix changed his key in early 1564; signs checked on the photographs, no label in doubt

outcome.notes: Catalogue 92 (part). R9241 read in part with de Foix's key; Status: in progress. R9238 moved to coligny1563 on 14 Oct 2026.

texts.label: R9241, Catherine de' Medici to Paul de Foix, 15 Jan 1563: Lawrence Beck's proposed reading (PR #18)
texts.summary: The Queen Mother writes to Paul de Foix, French ambassador in London, in de Foix's own cipher; the letter, copied by Patrick Forbes into his deciphering file (BL Add MS 4136), was evidently intercepted by the English. Beck's proposed partial decipherment speaks of the reconciliation needed between the two kingdoms, of how the negotiation goes, and of an aim to draw France into some outlay of money, 'dont nous n'avons nulle intention'. Partial, not at the read bar.
texts.note: Beck's proposed reading: passages B and D give connected clauses, but A and C have gaps or unresolved letter strings in most sentences (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026). Used 23 Oct 2026 (b19) as the base of the combined re-reading (third entry), which also stays below the bar.

texts.label: R9241: Feyseel Nur's graded reading with de Foix's 1565 key (PR #21)
texts.summary: An independent reading of the same letter with the frozen key from de Foix's 1565 cipher (Tomokiyo's chart, checked on BnF fr. 15971 ff. 21-26) plus a layer of values fitted on R9241, every reading graded. It converges with Beck's on phrases such as 'la negotiation prend quelque traict' and 'quelque deboursement de deniers'. The project's own transcriptions (first pass qm, second pass qm2) are listed; the exact 1,026-token token file the reading was decoded from is not separately in the folder.
texts.note: Nur's graded rendering with the 1565 key: dictionary fragments between ellipses, with conflicting values (r m/d, z p/i, Yb l/u) unresolved; no passage builds sentences (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026). Its frozen 1565 word signs (10, 26, 34, 40, 70, 82) are used in the b19 combined re-reading (third entry).

texts.label: R9241: combined re-reading, Beck's key with the 1565 word signs (b19, 23 Oct 2026)
texts.note: Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (b19): Beck's transcription and key v13 with the word signs of de Foix's 1565 cipher for the numbers he left open (10 dict, 26 bien, 34 tant, 40 faict, 70 toute, 82 ceulx, 37 me/car) and f = u twice; every trouble spot checked on the DECODE photographs (no label changed). Passages (2)-(4) build sentences with scattered holes; passage (1) breaks twice mid-sentence (A2, A14-A16), and B3, D7 and the closing name stay unread. Clean-sentence share of the body 0.361 on _check_reading.py (fr), 0.609 counting explicit holes only: below the bar, so decoded, not read, with the partial reading kept (texts/R9241_reading.md). Blocker: no-key-material (no 1563 decipherment of a de Foix letter; the open signs have no value in the 1565 chart).
